chunks: What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man whose garment was affected by janabah or blood.

He عليه السلام said: If he knew that janabah or blood had affected his garment before he performed salat, then he prayed in it and did not wash it, then he must repeat what he prayed. But if he thought that something had affected it, then he looked and did not see anything, it suffices for him to sprinkle it with water.

key_terms.بِالْمَاءِ: with water, the means of purification mentioned here
key_terms.ثَوْبَهُ: his garment, the object on which the impurity is found
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: major ritual impurity affecting the garment in this ruling
key_terms.دَمٌ: blood, a source of najasah mentioned in the narration
key_terms.يَغْسِلْهُ: to wash it, meaning purify the garment from impurity
key_terms.يَنْضَحَهُ: to sprinkle it, meaning to apply water lightly
key_terms.يُعِيدَ: to repeat, referring to repeating the salat

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone prays in clothes containing najasah before realizing it or after knowing it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about praying in a garment affected by najasah. If a person knew of janabah or blood on the garment before salat and still prayed without washing it, he must repeat the prayer; but if he only suspected something and found nothing upon inspection, sprinkling water on it is sufficient.
